entry.title: Ellipsoid Separation in Data-Dependent Time via Infimal Displacement Vectors
entry.summary: The infimal displacement vector of the nonexpansive operator underlying the primal-dual hybrid gradient algorithm (PDHG) is known to encode useful information for infeasible optimization problems. In particular, for the ellipsoid separation problem (ESP), where the goal is to find a separating hyperplane between two collections of ellipsoids, the infimal displacement vector corresponding to an infeasible second-order cone program (SOCP) encodes a separating hyperplane. We show FISTA computes a sequence of approximations to the dual component of the infimal displacement vector and establish that a solution to the ESP can be obtained in $\mathcal{O}(δ_{\mathcal{A}}^{-2})$ iterations. Here $δ_{\mathcal{A}}$ denotes the distance between the convex hulls of the two ellipsoid collections.

entry.title: Virtual defect mediated quantum melting in supersolids
entry.summary: The current understanding of supersolid melting is largely based on mean-field theories predicting that such transitions arise from a structural energy minimization mechanism. Here, we show that soft-core quasi-one-dimensional supersolids stabilized by a shallow external lattice can instead melt at zero temperature into a superfluid phase with quasi-long-range positional order through the proliferation of virtual soliton--antisoliton pairs, leading to a Kosterlitz--Thouless transition. We derive the corresponding Renormalization Group equations from first principles and use them to determine the critical properties of the system. Remarkably, the proliferation of topological defects near criticality strongly renormalizes both the density modulation and the superfluidity behavior. The transition described is intrinsically a beyond mean-field effect, since the external lattice produces only a smooth crossover between weakly and strongly modulated states at the mean-field level.

entry.title: Bi-Objective Receding-Horizon Scheduling of Nurses and Hospital Service Robots
entry.summary: This paper studies the joint scheduling of nurses and hospital service robots as a bi-objective mixed-integer linear programming problem. The formulation represents heterogeneous nursing skills, alternative skill-coverage modes, nurse availability and temporal rules, workload balance, robot task capability, charging and battery dynamics, and human supervision. Robot workload relief is credited only when an eligible service is actually executed, and explicit supervision-load variables deduct the corresponding nurse capacity from clinical coverage. The receding-horizon formulation also includes a cross-window night--morning constraint and a terminal battery reserve. The computational study is presented as numerical verification on synthetic hospital-like instances rather than clinical validation. Under the proposed formulation, the eight-nurse reference case gives $Z_1=0.78$ and $Z_2=3.164$. A common-budget comparison on B20 seed~1 yields total shortage $53.70$ for the integrated model, compared with $58.03$ for sequential nurse--robot scheduling and $59.46$ for the nurse-only baseline. Additional experiments examine multiple epsilon budgets on a larger B30 instance, sensitivity to robot-relief/supervision parameters and objective weights, and one-day versus two-day rolling horizons against a static full-horizon reference. The battery and routing representations remain aggregate planning approximations, and the scalability evidence is interpreted accordingly. No patient records or real hospital staff data are used, so the results establish model behavior and comparative numerical evidence rather than practical clinical effectiveness.

entry.title: Reconstruction differences rival individual differences in the fly compass connectome and break trained circuit models
entry.summary: Neural network models are increasingly constructed from synapse-resolution connectomes, and the same circuit is now available in reconstructions from other animals and pipelines. We do not know whether such models are dependent on the reconstruction they are built from, and whether connectome differences are biological or measurement errors. We studied the Drosophila head-direction circuit in nine versions: four flies (male CNS, hemibrain, FlyWire, BANC) and five variants of the same fly varying only by thresholds, proofreading or synapse detection. Using wiring-based correspondences validated by anatomical labels, we place all differences on one scale. A change of synapse detection within one fly changed the circuit more than halfway to the smallest between-fly difference on four distance measures; proofreading differences were smaller but depended on the metric, and left and right halves of one fly differed no more than random halves. Networks trained on each wiring to hold a cued heading developed near-perfect ring attractors, but their error increased from below 1 degree to 10-28 degrees when all weights changed by 1%. Training on each wiring did not transfer to any other connectome, including other versions of the same fly; refitting thirty cell-type gains, we repaired filtering-level differences but remaining error depended on wiring distance. Training with noise lowered precision and gave only partial transfer. In imaging data, the fly compass drifted gradually in darkness. Connectome-constrained models should report the reconstruction they were built on and be tested for robustness across reconstructions.

entry.title: Ask to Learn: Query-Based Collaborative Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary: Offline reinforcement learning is fundamentally limited by the coverage of the available data, while collecting additional trajectories through online exploration may be costly, unsafe, or infeasible. We study whether this limitation can be overcome without directly interacting with the underlying environment. Motivated by practical settings such as collaborator-mediated simulation, where a collaborator can provide information complementary to the offline data, we introduce query-based collaborative reinforcement learning to study how to acquire this information efficiently. The learner starts with a fixed offline dataset and adaptively queries state-time pairs; the collaborator samples an action according to a fixed, possibly suboptimal policy, and the simulator returns the corresponding reward and next state. For finite-horizon tabular problems, we derive an instance-dependent information-theoretic lower bound on the additional queries required to identify an $ε$-optimal policy and develop a local quadratic approximation. Guided by this characterization, we develop an adaptive query-allocation algorithm whose query complexity nearly matches the local benchmark under suitable conditions. Experiments on multiple synthetic and semi-synthetic environments demonstrate the empirical efficiency of the proposed method.

entry.title: Probing Graviton Mass with MeerKAT PTA and SKA-PTA Forecasts
entry.summary: In this study, we derive constraints on the graviton mass using the 4.5-year data release from the MeerKAT Pulsar Timing Array (MPTA) and provide forecasts for the upcoming Square Kilometre Array PTA (SKA-PTA). By modeling the modified dispersion relation and the corresponding tensor correlation function for massive gravitons, we perform Bayesian inference on the angular-correlation measurements under three noise configurations. Our 90\% credible upper limits on the graviton mass span $m_g < (2.10$-$2.58) \times 10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$. Including monopolar and dipolar contributions does not significantly alter these bounds, confirming that the constraints are driven by the quadrupolar tensor correlation. All results remain fully consistent with general relativity. For SKA-PTA, we forecast sensitivities down to $m_g \sim 10^{-24}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ with a 10-year observing baseline and $m_g \sim 10^{-25}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ with a 50-year observing baseline, representing order-of-magnitude improvements over current limits. This work demonstrates the power of current and future PTA observations to test fundamental aspects of gravity in the nanohertz band.

entry.title: Measurements on the separated subsystems of an entangled state
entry.summary: The entangled states of composite quantum systems are well studied. The particle-like nature of these systems also means that, while entangled, they can be physically separated and measurements performed on the separated subsystems. Measurements on the separated subsystems A and B should pertain to vectors in the local Hilbert space of each subsystem, but to date it has not been clear how to elucidate the relevant states of the separated subsystems because it is not obvious how to resolve them from states given in the tensor product basis, except for the separable states. Here it is shown that the projections of any general entangled state that are detected by measurements on the separated subsystems can be obtained considering the corresponding (cosets of) states in the free vector space from which the tensor product space is defined. The result eliminates the need to invoke random collapse, and from this perspective nonlocality arises because of the way measurements on each separated subsystem projects possible measurement outcomes.

entry.title: Graded Algebras over Polynomial Rings
entry.summary: Given a trivially graded polynomial ring $P_0=K[a_1,\dots,a_m]$ over a field $K$ and a positively graded polynomial ring $P=P_0[x_1,\dots,x_s]$, we study graded rings $R=P/I$, where $I$ is a homogeneous ideal of $P$ satisfying $I\cap P_0=\{0\}$. The induced morphism $Θ: {\rm Spec}(R)\rightarrow {\rm Spec}(P_0) = \mathbb{A}^m_K$ is used to prove that ${\rm Spec}(R)$ is connected. Next, we characterize and compute the following loci in $\mathbb{A}^m_K$: the set ${\rm Sing}_0(Θ)$ of all points whose corresponding point in the zero section of $Θ$ is singular in ${\rm Spec}(R)$, the set ${\rm Sing}_v(Θ)$ of all points $Γ$ such that the origin of the fiber $F_Γ$ of $Θ$ is singular, and the set ${\rm Sing}_s(Θ)$ of all points $Γ$ such that $\dim({\rm Sing}(F_Γ))\ge 1$. Finally, we apply these results to MaxDeg border basis schemes. Their coordinate rings are non-negatively graded by the total arrow degree and satisfy the above hypotheses. In particular, we explicitly determine the singular loci of the $\mathcal{O}$-border basis schemes with $\mathcal{O} = \{1,x,y,z,z^2\}$ and $\mathcal{O} = \{1,x,y,z,yz\}$.

entry.title: Fantastic Pretraining Optimizers and Where to Find Them II: Hyperball Optimization
entry.summary: Matrix based optimizers such as Muon can substantially speed up language model pretraining, but their gains over AdamW are observed to shrink as model size and data scale grow when using standard constant decoupled weight decay. We propose Hyperball, a simple optimizer wrapper that addresses this issue. Given a base optimizer such as Adam or Muon, Hyperball sets the Frobenius norms of weight matrices and their corresponding optimizer updates to fixed constants. On Qwen3 style models up to 1.2B parameters, Muon Hyperball achieves 20--30% token equivalent speedup over weight decay baselines. Hyperball also improves learning rate transfer across widths and depths compared to decoupled weight decay. This method is motivated by prior theory showing that training with weight decay leads to an equilibrium weight norm that only depends on the training hyperparameters. Through this mechanism, the weight decay then decides the angular learning rate, i.e. how fast the direction of the weight matrix changes.

entry.title: Quantum Reference Fields Transformations in Linearized Quantum Gravity
entry.summary: Diffeomorphism invariance is a central feature of general relativity. Without external reference structures, matter and geometry must be specified relationally, with respect to internal subsystems serving as reference frames. In quantum gravity, these reference systems must themselves be treated as quantum, motivating the use of quantum reference frames. In this work, we address how such a relational description could be formulated within linearized quantum gravity. To this purpose, we introduce quantum reference fields, i.e.,sets of four dynamical scalar fields whose stress-energy tensors enter the gravitational constraints. These fields extend the notion of quantum reference frames to local field-theoretic reference systems, allowing matter and gravitational degrees of freedom to be described relationally with respect to physical quantum systems whose states cannot be sharply peaked on definite field configurations. By generalizing the perspective-neutral construction of quantum reference frames, we show that relational, gauge invariant observables admit reduced descriptions in the perspective of each quantum reference field, and we derive the unitary transformations relating them. The resulting unitary maps implement local quantum coordinate changes between different internal perspectives, and act on the linearized gravitational field with an analogous structure to a linearized diffeomorphism, but with the classical gauge parameter replaced by a physical quantum field. Finally, we construct a relational von Neumann-type measurement scheme, showing how the corresponding reduced observables can be accessed operationally from the perspective of a quantum reference field.

entry.title: AlignFlow: Improving Flow-based Generative Models with Semi-Discrete Optimal Transport
entry.summary: Flow-based Generative Models (FGMs) effectively transform noise into complex data distributions. Incorporating Optimal Transport (OT) to couple noise and data during FGM training has been shown to improve the straightness of flow trajectories, enabling more effective inference. However, existing OT-based methods estimate the OT plan using (mini-)batches of sampled noise and data points, which limits their scalability to large and high-dimensional datasets in FGMs. This paper introduces AlignFlow, a novel approach that leverages Semi-Discrete Optimal Transport (SDOT) to enhance the training of FGMs by establishing an explicit, optimal alignment between noise distribution and data points with guaranteed convergence. SDOT computes a transport map by partitioning the noise space into Laguerre cells, each mapped to a corresponding data point. During FGM training, i.i.d. noise samples are paired with data points via the SDOT map. AlignFlow scales well to large datasets and model architectures with negligible computational overhead. Experimental results show that AlignFlow improves the performance of a wide range of state-of-the-art FGM algorithms and can be integrated as a plug-and-play component. Code is available at: https://github.com/konglk1203/AlignFlow.

entry.title: Ambiguous Fits: The Rashomon Effect and Challenges in Scaling Law Estimation
entry.summary: Estimating neural scaling laws involves an end-to-end pipeline: designing a scaling recipe, training models across scales, evaluating models on a target metric, and deploying an algorithm to fit a scaling law to the resulting data. This final fitting stage is often treated as routine: standard procedures minimize a non-convex fitting loss using local optimization from a grid of initializations, and return the best solution found. Yet such heuristic searches can fail in two distinct ways: they offer no guarantee of returning a nearly optimal solution, and they obscure whether fundamentally different parameter choices fit the data nearly as well. Indeed, we show that standard scaling law fitting is subject to a Rashomon effect (Breiman, 2001): the sublevel sets of near-minimizers correspond to broad parameter regions whose extrapolations diverge substantially at scale. We resolve these issues with a deterministic branch-and-bound algorithm that guarantees nearly optimal fitting loss and exhaustively maps the near-minimizers to the implied range of scaling curves.

entry.title: Spectra, Growth, and Localization in Half-Bounded Tensor Triangular Geometry
entry.summary: Over a noetherian scheme, classical cohomological support determines thick tensor ideals of perfect complexes. In half-bounded derived categories, complexes with the same support can generate different radical thick tensor ideals. We study how these distinctions affect the Balmer spectrum and localization. For a commutative noetherian ring $R$, we prove that $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(R))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian. For a nonempty noetherian scheme $X$, the corresponding condition is $\dim X=0$. For such a ring $R$ and a finite group $G$, $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(RG))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian and $|G|$ is invertible in $R$. Using the Sanders--Zhang classification over a discrete valuation ring, we compare objects whose annihilator exponents grow at different rates in different degrees. We lift the relevant generation relations before changing coefficients and obtain spectral retractions. These comparisons persist after thick quotients and algebraic localization under explicit uniform annihilation and nonvanishing conditions. A second argument uses nonnilpotent classes of positive degree and passes from cyclic subgroups to finite groups. Applications include relative results for schemes and bounded-below spectra with degreewise finitely generated homotopy. We also describe the cohomological information shared by the resulting ideals. The localization comparisons for bounded-below complexes of finitely generated modules and for bounded-below derived objects with finitely generated cohomology are established separately.

entry.title: Amplitude-Dependent Damping of Gravity--Capillary Waves in Power-Law Fluids: An Energy-Dissipation Framework
entry.summary: Classical gravity--capillary theory locates the restoring-force crossover, but the wave amplitudes and depths for which energy losses remain measurable depend on the constitutive response and on where viscous dissipation occurs. We develop a weak-loss mechanical-energy model for small-steepness progressive surface waves in memoryless power--law liquids. The full invariant of the leading inviscid strain field yields the deep-water bulk law $\dd A/\dd t=-C_tA^n$, with $C_t=4Kk^2(2kΩ)^{n-1}/[(n+1)ρ]$, and the corresponding spatial law $\dd A/\dd x=-(C_t/v_g)A^n$. For finite depth we calculate bulk dissipation using a phase- and depth-resolved quadrature $J_n(kh)$ and formulate a separate oscillatory power--law bottom layer. We solve the latter numerically in periodic state, obtaining dimensionless integrated wall losses $I_{0.6}\simeq0.5432$ and $I_{1.4}\simeq0.4708$ and recovering the exact Newtonian benchmark $I_1=1/2$. These values make it possible to evaluate conditional finite-depth bulk--wall dominance boundaries rather than only their amplitude exponents. The theory is organized into restoring-force, attenuation, local propagation-length, and dissipation-mechanism regime maps; at fixed wave steepness it additionally predicts a capillary-side maximum of normalized temporal damping for $0<n<2/3$. Grid, time-step, domain, and energy-work checks support the reduced wall calculation, while the coupled bulk--wall approximation still requires independent free-surface numerical or experimental validation. The results provide a reproducible single-fluid reference for subsequent two-liquid interfacial-wave modeling.

entry.title: Robust Observability for Schrödinger Equations with Singular Potentials on 2D Compact Hyperbolic Surfaces
entry.summary: This paper investigates the robustness of quantum observability on compact hyperbolic surfaces subject to $L^q$ potential perturbations with $2<q\leq \infty$. Since $L^q$ regularity is strictly subcritical in dimension two, for every non-empty open set $Ω\subset M$ and $T>0$, the solution of $(i\partial_t+Δ-V)u=0$ satisfies the space-time observability estimate $$ \|u_0\|_{L^2(M)}^2 \leq C\int_0^T \|e^{-it(-Δ+V)}u_0\|_{L^2(Ω)}^2\,dt. $$ A cornerstone of our analysis is Sogge's spectral cluster estimate, which allows us to obtain refined spectrally localized semiclassical Strichartz estimates adapted to rough potentials and to show that the potential's contribution vanishes in the propagation of semiclassical measures. The full-support property of invariant semiclassical measures on hyperbolic surfaces associated with the eigenfunctions then yields the desired observability by contradiction. By the Hilbert Uniqueness Method, the corresponding internal controllability result follows.

entry.title: $(p,q)$-weighted dual curvature measures
entry.summary: We study (p,q)-weighted dual curvature measures associated with a fixed nonnegative locally integrable Borel density satisfying a trace-regularity condition. These measures arise naturally from a variational formula for Wulff shapes. We establish the trace-regularity condition when g is pointwise α-homogeneous for some α\in R, or when g is radially non-increasing and continuous. For nontrivial even densities in either class, we prove existence results for the even version of the associated Minkowski problem under suitable assumptions. We also establish uniqueness when the prescribed measure has finite support, under a strict positivity assumption on the density and additional restrictions on the parameters. In the case of Lebesgue measure, our curvature measures reduce to those introduced by Lutwak, Yang, and Zhang, and our variational formulas recover their corresponding variational formula. For Gaussian measure, our results are related to those of Feng, Hu, and Xu, and Feng, Li, and Xu. Finally, we investigate the affine properties of the new measures and the associated mixed volumes.

entry.title: Sharp gradient comparison and rigidity for semilinear equations on manifolds
entry.summary: We prove sharp amplitude and gradient comparisons for positive solutions of a class of semilinear elliptic equations on complete manifolds under a Ricci lower bound. Equality at one point characterizes hyperbolic space and the corresponding radial solution. The local estimates are uniform in the mixing coefficients and number of terms for positive mixtures of subcritical powers. For a class of conformal compactifications defined by a source equation, we obtain sharp boundary scalar-curvature bounds and hyperbolic rigidity. We also construct non-Einstein examples whose normalization persists under small compactly supported metric perturbations.

entry.title: Finite-sum Identities and Supercongruences for Cubes of Catalan Numbers
entry.summary: Let $C_k=\binom{2k}{k}/(k+1)$ be the $k$-th Catalan number, and let $p$ be an odd prime. We establish exact finite-sum identities that, together with known binomial supercongruences and reductions of Sun, yield $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{16^k}\equiv2-24y^2-\frac{5p^2}{2y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+3y^2\equiv1\pmod3$, and $\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{C_k^3}{(-8)^k}\equiv-1-48y^2-\frac{33p^2}{16y^2}\pmod{p^3}$ when $p=x^2+4y^2\equiv1\pmod4$. We also evaluate the corresponding sum with denominator $16^k(k+1)^2$, and obtain two weighted Catalan supercongruences. The finite identities follow from the ratios of consecutive summands, symmetry of double sums, and telescoping. All endpoint terms are retained over the rational numbers before any modular reduction. In each bilinear identity, one endpoint denominator equals $p$; its cancellation produces the necessary term of order $p^2$. The precise arithmetic inputs are stated separately.

entry.title: From Speech Tokens to Stolen Voices: Attacker-Chosen-Text Speaker Impersonation via Representation Inversion
entry.summary: Speech interaction systems have gradually evolved from traditional cascaded systems that use text as intermediate information to end-to-end speech language models that directly process speech representations. In some applications, the speech frontend runs on the user's device and sends speech representations to a remote server for inference, while the original audio remains local. However, these representations may still contain speaker identity information. If an attacker obtains them, it may use this information to imitate the user's voice, threatening their voice privacy. To investigate this risk, we propose \stia, a Speech Token Inversion Attack that generates speech with attacker-specified text in a victim's voice using a single short leaked representation, without access to the original audio or its transcript. Specifically, \stia converts discrete, continuous, or mixed speech representations into conditioning sequences and trains a conditional flow-matching speech generation model using pairs of different utterances from the same speaker in public speech datasets. The model combines speaker characteristics contained in the leaked representation with the specified text to generate speech in the victim's voice. Experiments show that, with a Moshi representation leak corresponding to 3 seconds of speech, \stia achieves an average CAM++ speaker cosine similarity of 0.78 and a target-text word error rate of 3.80\%. These results show that speech frontend representations reveal reusable speaker identity information and highlight the need to consider privacy risks when designing speech frontend representation methods.

entry.title: Dynamics-Aware Sampling and Recovery for Tensor-Valued Dynamical Systems
entry.summary: We study sampling and recovery for tensor-valued dynamical systems evolving under the t-product, using partial spatial observations over time. Although the t-product Fourier transform yields slicewise matrix dynamics, recovery does not generally decouple across slices. Eigenvalues shared across Fourier-domain frontal slices couple the corresponding eigenspaces into aggregated spectral blocks, which determine the tensor-specific recovery geometry and space--time tradeoff. We establish deterministic identifiability conditions for the initial tensor state. In the diagonalizable case, these are frame conditions on the aggregated blocks. We extend them to non-diagonalizable systems through generalized eigenspaces and Jordan structure. A temporal--spectral factorization of the finite-horizon stacked recovery system underlying Tensor Dynamical Sampling (DS) yields a decoupled two-stage formulation once the temporal threshold is reached. Under independent spatial subsampling, we prove high-probability recovery guarantees using empirical Gram matrices on the aggregated blocks. The bounds depend on aggregated multiplicities, incoherence, and population conditioning. Stability estimates separate the spatial frame factor from the temporal Vandermonde factor and show that increasing temporal depth may worsen numerical conditioning even after identifiability is ensured. We implement Tensor DS and evaluate it on synthetic and real data. Phase transitions track the predicted blockwise sampling thresholds, and stability experiments illustrate Vandermonde conditioning. Experiments on sea surface temperature and turbulence velocity data show that a learned t-product system operator generally yields more accurate and structurally faithful reconstructions than vectorized low-rank, Tucker-type, graph-regularized, graph-spectral, and vectorized dynamical sampling baselines.

entry.title: Revisiting monodromy defects in $\text{O}(N)$ conformal field theories
entry.summary: Monodromy defects are fundamental objects in extended quantum systems with global symmetries. We study such defects in $\text{O}(N)$ conformal field theories (CFT), which describe the universality class of $\text{O}(N)$ spontaneous symmetry breaking transitions. In particular, we consider partial-monodromy defects, whose corresponding symmetry transformations only act on a subset of the fundamental $\text{O}(N)$ vector field. We develop an analytical theory of the defect phases, using both renormalization group and large $N$ expansion. In general (spacetime) dimensions $3\leq d<4$, multiple defect CFTs are identified, which are described by appropriate boundary conditions for the vector field near the defect. Near $d=3$, we show that in the large $N$ limit, a stable defect CFT always exists, characterized by the so-called ("standard") "alternate" boundary conditions for the (twisted) untwisted fields, whose defect correlations are (suppressed) enhanced. We then perform large-scale classical Monte Carlo simulations of monodromy defects in the O(3) CFT in an improved lattice model and numerically extract the defect scaling dimensions. The numerical results are in qualitative agreement with the stable defect CFT identified in the field theory.

entry.title: Knowledge distillation across teacher architectures for compact diabetic retinopathy grading
entry.summary: Diabetic retinopathy grading from retinal fundus photographs is important but difficult to deploy on resource-constrained hardware. We conducted a controlled study of offline response-based knowledge distillation for five-class diabetic retinopathy grading on APTOS 2019, comparing ResNet-50, MobileNetV3-Large, and Swin Transformer-Tiny (Swin-T) teachers distilled into a MobileNetV3-Small student. A 3 x 4 x 2 grid of teacher, temperature, and hard-label weight was screened at one seed, while six configurations and the no-distillation baseline were evaluated across three seeds. The highest observed single-seed quadratic weighted kappa was 0.9093 (macro-F1 0.6851) for Swin-T at temperature 4 and hard-label weight 0.7; the corresponding three-seed mean was 0.9024, compared with 0.8804 for the baseline. The student used 1.52 M parameters and 5.94 MB, representing an 18.07x parameter reduction relative to Swin-T. Temperature and hard-label weight effects were teacher- and configuration-dependent, while small performance differences were sensitive to random seed. Knowledge distillation produced a compact student with competitive performance under the evaluated protocol, but independent external validation remains necessary.

entry.title: New bound on $S_{1}\times S_{2}$-setting Bell locality of a nonseparable Werner state
entry.summary: In many quantum applications it is important to know whether or not a Bell nonlocal two-qudit state exhibits its nonlocality under correlation scenarios with some given numbers $S_{1},S_{2}\geq1$ of generalized quantum measurements at two sites. In the present article, we find analytically a new general condition sufficient for a nonseparable Werner state with a dimension $d\leq\min\{S_{1},S_{2}\}$ to satisfy all Bell inequalities under every $S_{1}\times S_{2}$-setting correlation scenario with outcomes of an arbitrary spectral type, discrete or continuous $-$ that is, to be $S_{1}\times S_{2}$-setting Bell local, for short. For a variety of measurement settings $S_{1}, S_{2}$, this new general bound is beyond (i) Werner's and Barrett's locality bounds for a nonseparable Werner state and (ii) the related result by Johnson and Viola [Phys. Rev. A 88, 032323 (2013)] on "sharability" of this state. When specialized to $d = 2$ and $\min\{S_{1},S_{2}\} = 2, 3$, our new general bound improves upon the corresponding results by Terhal et. al. in [Phys. Rev. Lett. 90, 157903 (2003)], moreover, for $d=\min\{S_{1},S_{2}\} = 2$, it reduces exactly to the bound derived for this case via the CHSH inequality. We prove also explicitly in operator terms the result of Terhal et. el. that every nonseparable Werner state with a dimension $d >\min\{S_{1},S_{2}\}$ is $S_{1}\times S_{2}$-setting Bell local. The new results presented in this article are important for both the theory of Bell nonlocality and quantum applications based on this fundamental concept.

entry.title: A Framework for Learning and Reliability Certification in Neural Polar Decoding
entry.summary: This paper investigates a framework that connects network training, independently certified population risk and sequential reliability in neural polar decoding. Network outputs determine information-bit decisions by their signs. Posterior mean-squared error (MSE) controls bit-error rate (BER), and a first-error identity connects errors evaluated with true preceding bits to sequential block-error rate (BLER). Three methods exploit sequential decoding structure to certify changes to trained receivers. First, distances from trained outputs to the zero decision threshold, termed learned margins, yield reliability bounds for over-parameterized neural network (ONN) updates subject to separate mean-squared output-change constraints at information positions. Second, a shared loss takes the largest block-error indicator difference between candidate decoders and successive cancellation (SC) on each frame. Its expectation bounds the corresponding BLER differences, termed excess BLER, for all fixed combinations of information-position implementations. An exact expression quantifies the gap between this shared bound and the largest BLER difference among fixed decoders. Third, verified linear programming (LP) and candidate-set subdivision tighten these guarantees with controllable computation at fixed confidence. ONN experiments assess conditional fitting and weight updates. Polar factor-graph experiments demonstrate reusable combination guarantees and storage reduction under prescribed excess-BLER allowances. Component timing identifies the dominant graph-propagation cost.

entry.title: Forecasting Ionospheric Irregularities on GNSS Lines of Sight Using Dynamic Graphs with Ephemeris Conditioning
entry.summary: Most data-driven ionospheric models operate on gridded products, which do not preserve the time-varying sampling structure of satellite-based sensing. We instead model the ionosphere as a dynamic graph over ionospheric pierce points, with connectivity that evolves as satellite positions change. Because satellite trajectories are predictable, the graph topology over the forecast horizon can be constructed in advance. We exploit this property to condition forecasts on the future graph structure, which we term ephemeris conditioning. This enables prediction on lines of sight (LoS) that appear only in the forecast horizon. We evaluate our framework on Global Navigation Satellite System data from a co-located receiver pair in Singapore spanning 2023 to 2025. The task is forecasting irregularities defined by the Rate of TEC Index (ROTI) up to 2 hours ahead as per-node binary classification. The resulting model, IonoDGNN, achieves a Brier Skill Score (BSS) of 0.55 and an area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC) of 0.77. These correspond to improvements over persistence of 53% in BSS and 58% in PR-AUC, with larger gains at longer lead times. Ablations confirm that graph structure and ephemeris conditioning each contribute meaningfully. Under simulated coverage dropout, the model retains predictive skill on affected nodes through spatial message passing from observed neighbors. Compared to interpolation baselines, the proposed model achieves better recovery, especially at higher dropout levels. These results suggest that dynamic graph forecasting on evolving LoS is a viable alternative for ionospheric modeling. The project and the dataset are available at https://github.com/Mert-chan/IonoDGNN.

entry.title: Two-qubit binegativity can increase under local amplitude damping
entry.summary: It has been conjectured that the binegativity of two-qubit states is an entanglement monotone. We present a full-rank state as a counterexample: applying amplitude damping to only one of the qubits can increase the binegativity of the state. The output state remains full rank, and the amount of increase can be calculated exactly. In addition, we construct a family of counterexamples that vary continuously with a parameter. In the corresponding one-way local operations and classical communication protocol, the probability-weighted average of the binegativity over the branches after the local measurement is also higher than that of the initial state.

entry.title: A marked scheme representation for Voronoi volumes in the Brownian map
entry.summary: For any fixed number $k\ge3$ of independent volume-sampled sites in the unit-area Brownian map, we represent the negative-power transform of their ordinary Voronoi volumes as a finite sum of marked planar scheme integrals. These integrals arise from the critical asymptotics of generating functions for face-constrained labelled planar maps. To connect them to Voronoi volumes, we use Miermont's zero-delay correspondence to interpret the labelled maps as quadrangulations with distinguished sites and then pass to the Brownian map scaling limit.

entry.title: Bistable fronts in periodic media: phase reduction and realization of circle flows
entry.summary: We establish a phase reduction and a converse realization theorem for front dynamics in one-dimensional periodic reaction-diffusion-advection equations. For sufficiently large periods under local bistability, and sufficiently small periods when the homogenized equation admits a stationary front, we construct strictly ordered invariant front families that are normally exponentially attracting and locally complete for entire orbits. Modulo spatial-period translations, the dynamics on each family reduces exactly to a circle flow: rotations correspond to propagating pulsating fronts, equilibria to stationary fronts, and connecting orbits to transition fronts between stationary fronts. Conversely, every smooth circle flow can be realized, up to time-preserving topological conjugacy, as the quotient dynamics of such a family for a periodic, locally bistable equation with constant diffusion and no advection. Realizations with a Cantor set of stationary phases and a connecting orbit in each complementary interval illustrate the richness of front dynamics in these media. We also obtain first-order phase-velocity expansions in both period limits, quantitative propagation laws near zero frozen speed, and global exponential orbital stability of propagating pulsating fronts.

entry.title: AudioFM: Towards General Purpose Audio Representation Learning
entry.summary: Learning audio representations that effectively bridge holistic global soundscapes with fine-grained acoustic moments is a long-standing goal in self-supervised learning. Recording-level contrastive objectives encourage agreement between pooled audio representations, but do not explicitly supervise local time-frequency representations. We introduce AudioFM, a self-supervised framework that combines recording-level contrast with patch-wise masked latent discrimination. Using visible acoustic context, a student predicts representations of masked patches and identifies their corresponding full-view teacher targets among candidates from other recordings. We further incorporate weaker supervision from eligible temporal neighbors to encourage local temporal consistency. Extensive evaluations show that AudioFM achieves state-of-the-art performance across diverse audio domains in linear probing, fine-tuning, and zero-shot transfer, demonstrating superior event detection, robust scene-level understanding, and strong domain generalizability.

entry.title: U-VLM: Hierarchical Vision Language Modeling for Report Generation
entry.summary: Automated radiology report generation is key for reducing radiologist workload and improving diagnostic consistency, yet generating accurate reports for 3D medical imaging remains challenging. Existing vision-language models face two limitations: they do not leverage segmentation-pretrained encoders, and they inject visual features only at the input layer of language models, losing multi-scale information. We propose U-VLM, which enables hierarchical vision-language modeling in both training and architecture: (1) progressive training from segmentation to classification to report generation, and (2) multi-layer visual injection that routes U-Net encoder features to corresponding language model layers. Each training stage can leverage different datasets without unified annotations. U-VLM achieves state-of-the-art performance on CT-RATE (F1: 0.414 vs 0.258, BLEU-mean: 0.349 vs 0.305) and AbdomenAtlas 3.0 (F1: 0.624 vs 0.518 for segmentation-based detection) using only a 0.1B decoder trained from scratch, demonstrating that well-designed vision encoder pretraining outweighs the benefits of 7B+ pre-trained language models. Ablation studies show that progressive pretraining significantly improves F1, while multi-layer injection improves BLEU-mean. Code is available at https://github.com/yinghemedical/U-VLM.

entry.title: Intersecting integer partitions: star bounds and counterexamples at every scale
entry.summary: Two integer partitions $t$-intersect if they have at least $t$ common parts, counted with multiplicity. We study the largest $t$-intersecting families of integer partitions of $n$ into exactly $k$ positive parts. The canonical $t$-star consists of the partitions containing at least $t$ ones. Applying Kupavskii's weak-spread theorem, we prove that this star is largest whenever $n\ge Ak^3$, for every fixed $A>24$ and all sufficiently large $k$, uniformly over $1\le t<k$. We also give counterexamples to Borg's conjecture at every intersection scale: for all sufficiently large $k$ and for every $1\le t\le \lceil k/4\rceil$, we describe $t$-intersecting families on integer partitions of $n=\lfloor tk^2/3\rfloor$ into $k$ parts which are strictly larger than the corresponding canonical stars. Moreover we present a family of counterexamples to Borg's conjectures about largest $t$-intersecting families of integer partitions of $n$ without restricting the number of parts.

entry.title: Maximal Spaceability of the set of non-absolutely summing operators in quasi-Banach spaces
entry.summary: For every $0<p<1$, we establish maximal spaceability of the bounded operators on $\ell_p$ which fail to be $(r,s)$-absolutely summing for all $1\le s\le r<\infty$, using the coordinate-disjointization construction and Maddox's theorem. We give detailed isometric estimates and prove a corresponding maximal spaceability theorem inside the compact operators. The compact result is based on an explicit diagonal multiplier and a single weakly $1$-summable sequence witnessing the simultaneous failure of all admissible absolute summability conditions. A diagonal characterization, a logarithmic compact example, and extensions to operators with values in quasi-Banach spaces containing a copy of $\ell_p$ are also obtained. The constructed subspaces are isomorphic to $\ell_p$ and have maximal algebraic dimension whenever the ambient operator spaces have dimension $\mathfrak c$.

entry.title: Sharp Quantitative Weighted Estimates for Lifted Maximal Operators with Applications
entry.summary: In this article, we establish sharp quantitative weighted estimates for the lifted Hardy--Littlewood (resp Sobolev sharp) maximal operators $\{\mathcal M_θ\}_{θ\in(0,\infty)}$ (resp $\{\mathcal M_θ^\sharp\}_{θ\in(0,\infty)}$). Specifically, for $p\in(1,\infty)$, $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, $\upsilon\in A_p$, and $f\in L^p_\upsilon$, we prove that \begin{align*} \sup_{θ,λ\in(0,\infty)}λ^p \underset{\mathcal M_θ(f)(x,t)>λt^γ} {\int_{\mathbb R^n}\int_0^\infty} t^{γp-1}\,dt\,\upsilon(x)\,dx \lesssim [\upsilon]_{A_p}^{α_{p,γ}} \|f\|_{L^p_\upsilon}^p, \end{align*} where $α_{p,γ}:=\frac{p}{p-1}$ for $γ\in[-n,0)$ and $α_{p,γ}:=1$ otherwise and where the implicit positive constant depends only on $n$, $p$, and $γ$. For $\mathcal M_θ^\sharp$, the corresponding estimate holds with $\|f\|_{L^p_\upsilon}^p$ replaced by $\|\nabla f\|_{L^p_\upsilon}^p$ for any $f\in\dot W^{1,p}_\upsilon$, and with $α_{p,γ}:=\frac{p}{p-1}$ for $γ\in[-1,0)$ and $α_{p,γ}:=1$ otherwise. We show that, for an $A_1$ weight $\upsilon$, the weight constant in the above estimates becomes $[\upsilon]_{A_1}$ for the sharp ranges $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, or $p=1$ and $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus[-n,0]$ (resp. $γ\in\mathbb R\setminus[-1,0]$). We also prove that $α_{p,γ}$ is sharp, and we establish exact limiting formulae and characterize Muckenhoupt weights via weak-type bounds. As applications, we characterize the weighted Hardy(--Sobolev) space $H^1_\upsilon$ with $\upsilon\in A_1$ in terms of the truncated Riesz transforms with optimal range $γ\in \mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$. More applications include the sharp weighted Caffarelli--Silvestre extension and the generalization to ball Banach function spaces.

entry.title: How High Can GPT-6 Astra Climb in Contact-Rich Manipulation? PhysLadder: A Hierarchical, Matched Sim-Real Benchmark for Physical Interaction
entry.summary: We introduce PhysLadder, a hierarchical Sim-Real benchmark for evaluating physical interaction capabilities in contact-rich manipulation. Its 16 household tasks span three cumulative levels: contact selection and geometric alignment (L1), force regulation within sustained contact (L2), and coordinated contact reconfiguration and force regulation (L3). Each task is instantiated in physically and visually matched simulated and real-world environments, with shared task definitions and success criteria. We evaluate GPT-6 Astra zero-shot with three trials per task in each environment. Real-world success rates decline from 80.0% at L1 to 47.6% at L2 and 0.0% at L3, with corresponding simulation rates of 66.7%, 47.6%, and 0.0%. Ten of the 16 tasks have identical success counts across environments; the remaining six differ by one success out of three trials. Across both environments, recurring difficulties in spatial reasoning, contact selection, force regulation, and coordination often prevent local physical progress from accumulating into task completion. These findings characterize Astra's observed capability boundary across increasing interaction demands and, for this model, support matched simulation as a repeatable, scalable testbed for studying the sustained, coordinated physical interactions that limit reliable manipulation.

entry.title: Geometric Eisenstein Series, Intertwining Operators, and Shin's Averaging Formula
entry.summary: In the geometric Langlands program over function fields, Braverman-Gaitsgory and Laumon constructed geometric Eisenstein functors which geometrize the classical construction of Eisenstein series. Fargues and Scholze very recently constructed a general candidate for the local Langlands correspondence, via a geometric Langlands correspondence occurring over the Fargues-Fontaine curve. We carry some of the theory of geometric Eisenstein series over to the Fargues-Fontaine setting. Namely, given a quasi-split connected reductive group $G/\mathbb{Q}_{p}$ with simply connected derived group and maximal torus $T$, we construct an Eisenstein functor $\mathrm{nEis}(-)$, which takes sheaves on $Bun_{T}$ to sheaves on $Bun_{G}$. We show that, given a sufficiently nice $L$-parameter $φ_{T}: W_{\mathbb{Q}_{p}} \rightarrow \phantom{}^{L}T$, there is a Hecke eigensheaf on $Bun_{G}$ with eigenvalue $φ$, given by applying $\mathrm{nEis}(-)$ to the Hecke eigensheaf $\mathcal{S}_{φ_{T}}$ on $Bun_{T}$ attached to $φ_{T}$ by Fargues and Zou. We show that $\mathrm{nEis}(\mathcal{S}_{φ_{T}})$ interacts well with Verdier duality, and, assuming compatibility of the Fargues-Scholze correspondence with a suitably nice form of the local Langlands correspondence, provide an explicit formula for the stalks of the eigensheaf in terms of parabolic inductions of the character $χ$ attached to $φ_{T}$. This has several surprising consequences. First, it recovers special cases of an averaging formula of Shin for the cohomology of local Shimura varieties with rational coefficients, and generalizes it to the non-minuscule case. Second, it refines the averaging formula in the cases where the parameter $φ$ is sufficiently nice, giving an explicit formula for the degrees of cohomology that certain parabolic inductions sit in, and this refined formula holds even with torsion coefficients.

entry.title: The Genus-One B-Model Calabi-Yau/Landau-Ginzburg Correspondence
entry.summary: Let $f:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $n$ with an isolated critical point at the origin. The Calabi--Yau/Landau--Ginzburg correspondence predicts a close relation between invariants of the Landau--Ginzburg orbifold $(\mathbb C^n/\mathbb Z_n,f)$ and those of the associated Calabi--Yau hypersurface $ X_f=\{[z_1:\cdots:z_n]\in\mathbb P^{n-1}:f(z_1,\ldots,z_n)=0\}. $ In this paper, we establish this correspondence for the genus-one B-model by constructing the Landau--Ginzburg genus-one B-model invariant intrinsically from the $f$-twisted Laplacian on $\mathbb{C}^n/\mathbb{Z}_n$ and proving that it agrees with the corresponding BCOV invariant of $X_f$ up to an additive constant depending only on the dimension.

entry.title: From the massive Schwinger model to unimodular Euclidean gravity with fermions
entry.summary: The massive Schwinger model (two-dimensional electrodynamics coupled to Dirac fermions) in Euclidean spacetime is mapped onto two-dimensional unimodular gravity in the first-order formalism, also including fermions. The idea of the map relies almost entirely on the isomorphism between the gauge groups $U(1)$ and $SO(2)$. However, the resulting fermion-gravity coupling differs from the conventional form, explicitly violating parity and time-reversal symmetries. Moreover, these fermions exhibit an unconventional transformation behavior under $SO(2)$ transformations. We show, however, that these properties are absent on the gravitational side of the mapping when starting from an axial massive Schwinger model. Several explicit examples of the mapping are considered, including the constant electric field and point-particle systems. For these examples, we explicitly derive the corresponding gravitational manifolds and compute the associated metrics. Furthermore, we analyze the consistency of the mapping at the quantum level using the path-integral formalism and Becchi-Rouet-Stora-Tyutin (BRST) techniques. Our results demonstrate that the proposed mapping remains consistent at the quantum level, establishing a formal BRST-compatible field correspondence between quantum electrodynamics and quantum gravity, at least at the $U(1) - SO(2)$ gauge sector, which does not include the diffeomorphic features of gravity.

entry.title: Structured Continuity Equations in Fibred Wasserstein Spaces
entry.summary: In this article, we develop a comprehensive ODE-theory for structured continuity equations in fibred probability spaces, which represent a class of heterogeneous PDEs arising as the meanfield limit of nonexchangeable particle systems. After investigating in depth the topologies induced by the so-called fibred (or conditional) and classical Wasserstein metrics on such probability spaces, we establish quantitative Cauchy-Lipschitz and qualitative Carathéodory-Peano well-posedness results for structured continuity equations, along with precise correspondences between this class of evolutions, classical Lagrangian dynamics, and continuity equations. In keeping with what has long been known for exchangeable dynamics, we derive a general meanfield approximation result by solutions of nonexchangeable particle systems, along with a quantitative variant thereof under practically reasonable regularity assumptions on the driving field and initial data.

entry.title: Residual-Calibrated Multimodal Spatiotemporal Learning for Future Beam Prediction
entry.summary: We propose a residual calibrated multimodal spatiotemporal framework for future beam prediction on DeepSense 6G Scenario 23. The framework integrates visual observations, location features, and historical beam labels to predict the beam label of the next dataset record. A pretrained Swin-Tiny encoder extracts features from four consecutive RGB frames. Bidirectional cross-attention integrates visual and two dimensional Unit 1 location representations, while a temporal Transformer incorporates historical beam label embeddings to model dependencies across the observation window. A supplementary offline residual head adjusts the frozen supervised logits using immediate correctness rewards and an auxiliary classification loss. A fixed probability mixture of the supervised and residual outputs is selected using validation accuracy. From 11,387 aligned records, we construct 11,255 temporal windows and partition them by capture run into 7,854 training, 1,905 validation, and 1,496 test samples. The supervised predictor achieves Top-1, Top-2, Top-3, and Top-5 test accuracies of 62.83%, 74.80%, 79.75%, and 81.08%, respectively. The residual predictor achieves corresponding accuracies of 61.76%, 75.07%, 79.41%, and 81.02%. Residual adjustment increases Top-2 accuracy by 0.27 percentage points, while the supervised predictor retains higher Top-1, Top-3, and Top-5 accuracies. The validation-selected mixture coincides with the residual predictor. The proposed framework combines cross-modal sensing features with explicit beam-history conditioning and a separately trained residual adjustment stage for one-record-ahead beam prediction. Initial evaluation on held-out capture runs characterizes the candidate-ranking performance of both prediction stages and favors the supervised variant for Top-1 selection. These findings motivate further study of historical conditioning and residual refinement.

entry.title: Approximating the Euclidean Ball by Polytopes: Surprising Rates in High Dimensions
entry.summary: We determine the sharp dimensional dependence of the asymptotic approximation error for the Euclidean unit ball $B_2^d\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ by polytopes with a prescribed number of vertices in the relative symmetric difference metric. Specifically, we prove that $$\lim_{N\to\infty}N^{2/(d-1)}\inf_{P\in P_d(N)}\frac{\operatorname{vol}_d(P\triangle B_2^d)}{\operatorname{vol}_d(B_2^d)}=Θ(d^{-1/2}),$$ where $P_d(N)$ consists of polytopes with at most $N$ vertices and no containment restriction. Equivalently, the classical Laguerre-Delone triangulation numbers satisfy $\operatorname{ldel}_{d-1}=Θ(d^{-1/2})$. This improves the lower bound $Ω(d^{-1})$ of Böröczky (2000) and the upper bound $O(1)$ of Ludwig, Schütt and Werner (2006). In contrast, the corresponding asymptotic coefficient for approximation with a prescribed number of facets has order one, as shown by Kur (2020). We also establish non-asymptotic bounds showing that, for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, the ball admits an $\varepsilon$-approximation with at most $\exp(C(\varepsilon)\sqrt d)$ vertices, whereas approximating the hypercube to the same accuracy requires at least $\exp(c(\varepsilon)d)$ vertices. Consequently, the ball does not maximize the optimal relative approximation error among convex bodies, even up to an absolute multiplicative constant at the same vertex budget. Thus Macbeath's theorem (1951) on the extremality of the ball for inscribed approximation does not extend to polytopes in arbitrary position.

entry.title: From Slices to Volumes: Comparing 2D, 2.5D, and 3D Residual Networks for Pulmonary Nodule Malignancy-Risk Classification
entry.summary: Purpose: To compare 2D, 2.5D, and 3D residual networks for pulmonary nodule malignancy-risk classification and evaluate momentum-contrast pretraining, mild augmentation, and exclusion of indeterminate ratings. Methods: A retrospectively prepared LIDC-IDRI cohort contained 2,654 nodules labeled benign, indeterminate, or malignant using median radiologist ratings. Patient-disjoint splits comprised 1,876 training, 382 validation, and 396 test nodules. Representations included one axial slice, five neighboring slices, and a local CT volume. Each track evaluated a randomly initialized baseline, momentum-contrast pretraining followed by fine-tuning, and supervised training with mild augmentation. Checkpoints were selected by validation Macro-F1. The 2D experiments used three seeds; 2.5D and 3D results were single-run estimates. A separate binary experiment excluded indeterminate nodules. Results: Augmented models achieved test Macro-F1 values of $0.6134\pm0.0075$ for 2D, $0.6537$ for 2.5D, and $0.5403$ for 3D; the 2D uncertainty denotes population standard deviation across seeds. Corresponding accuracies were $0.6128$, $0.6869$, and $0.5455$. Augmentation improved Macro-F1 within every track, whereas the tested pretraining recipes reduced it. Binary Macro-F1 values were $0.8227$, $0.8664$, and $0.7554$, respectively. Conclusion: Augmented 2.5D achieved the highest observed performance. Differences in preprocessing, optimization, capacity, and replication limit attribution to dimensionality. Labels reflect radiologist-assessed malignancy risk rather than pathology-confirmed cancer. Code and experimental results are available at https://github.com/CT-DeepLearning-Team/CT-2D-2.5D-3D-DeepLearning.

entry.title: Planetesimal Delivery to Giant Planet Circumplanetary Disks: Bulk Ice Enrichment and an Ice-rich Iapetus
entry.summary: The regular satellites of Jupiter and Saturn are substantially enriched in ice relative to the rock-rich solids of the outer Solar System. In addition, the satellites interior to Titan and distant Iapetus are icier than Titan itself. Collisional processes and subsequent migration can readily alter compositions deep in the planetary potential well, but producing a distant, ice-rich satellite with Iapetus's radius of about 700 km is a challenge \citep{mosqueira2026a}. We show that differential ablation and capture of icy and rocky fragments from differentiated outer Solar System bodies can explain the bulk Jovian and Kronian satellite ice enrichment and supply the substantial ice-rich inventory needed for Iapetus. For 1\,m--1\,km fragments with the canonical size-distribution index \(p=3.5\) and a source containing 30\% ice by mass, the fixed radial distance Saturn calculation deposits material with ice fractions of 0.66 (delivery of vapor-only rock) or 0.50 (with retained rock melt) at 20 Saturn radii and nearly pure ice at 60 Saturn radii. Following three-dimensional trajectories over repeated passages through the pressure-supported gas gives ice fractions of about 0.4 near 20 Saturn radii and 0.9 near 60 Saturn radii. The matching Jupiter calculation yields a similar bulk ice enrichment, with a corresponding compositional gradient across the Galilean satellite region. These delivery profiles supply ice-enriched material for satellite formation. Yet satellitesimal inward migration subsequently modifies the material incorporated into satellites and thus alters their bulk compositions. We briefly discuss the implications for the PDS~70 planetary system.

entry.title: Lifting $τ$-exceptional sequences
entry.summary: We study the behaviour of $τ$-exceptional sequences under passage from a finite-dimensional algebra $Λ$ to a factor algebra $Λ/I$. Assuming that $Λ$ is $τ$-tilting finite and that $I\subseteq \operatorname{rad}Λ$, we construct, for every $r$ less than or equal to the number of simple $Λ$-modules, an injective map from the $τ$-exceptional sequences of length $r$ over $Λ/I$ to those over $Λ$. The construction is recursive and is based on lifting indecomposable $τ$-rigid modules and comparing their associated $τ$-perpendicular categories. At each stage, we construct a right exact functor between the relevant $τ$-perpendicular categories which, after identifying them with module categories, is naturally isomorphic to extension of scalars along a quotient $Γ\toΓ/J$, where $J\subseteq \operatorname{rad}Γ$. These functors send each lifted term to an object in the additive closure of the corresponding original term. Finally, we conjecture connections with known bijections for representations of quivers over local algebras and for Nakayama algebras.
